summary: Icon tweak verified by pixel analysis (/app/tests/check_icon_v2.py recreates the background from draw_icon_v2.py and diffs it). icon.png 1024x1024 RGB; figure alpha ends at row 815 (line is rows ~806-815); rows >=818 have zero figure pixels; the only difference from the pure background below the line is the intentional soft halo blur (max diff 26 at y=818, fading to 5 by y=838). Bodies are domes with no straight vertical segment. adaptive-icon.png 1024 RGBA: every pixel with alpha>8 sits within 312.6px of centre (0 px beyond 313), bbox x257-766, y365-695. Home screen (390x844, onboarded=true) shows home-logo (56x56, icon.png loaded, naturalWidth 1024) with 0 console errors.

issues: body() draws exactly the upper HALF of the ellipse (chord 180-360 with ellipse height 2h), so the floor cuts it at the equator where the tangent is vertical. The bottom ~50px look almost vertical: left body x goes 172->165 between y=750 and y=804. The user may still read this as 'vertical sides'. Optional fix: make the ellipse taller than 2h, or move its centre below the floor (e.g. top + 2.6*h with the floor still cutting it), so the shoulders meet the line at a slant.

action_items: Optional: if the user still sees vertical sides, cut the ellipse above its equator so the body edges meet the floor line at a slant (see design_issues).
critical_code_review_comments: draw_icon_v2.py: the halo is applied to the whole figure, so a faint glow (<=26/255 diff) shows just below the floor line. This is by design, not body pixels.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run python /app/tests/check_icon_v2.py (~60s) to recheck icon pixels. Floor line sits at 1024-px rows ~806-815. Adaptive art is 660px pasted at (182,170).
